messages:
zara: quick thread — ran a mixed-precision bakeoff (FP8/INT8/AWQ/GPTQ) for rwd-llama-7b-v2 on H100 and L40S; bumped into a weird attention-scale drift on L40S when seq > 4k. short notes below.

samir: can you paste the exact commands and config you used?

zara: sure — minimal reproduce 
```
./bakeoff --model rwd-llama-7b-v2 --devices h100,l40s --quant-modes fp8,int8,awq,gptq --batch 1 --seq-len 8192 --warmup 200 --prompts-file tests/longseq_prompts.jsonl --log-level debug
```

zara: results summary (token-level BLEU-ish deltas vs fp32 baseline):
- H100: FP8 ~ -0.25% perf, INT8 ~ -0.9%, AWQ ~ -1.4%, GPTQ ~ -0.8%
- L40S: FP8 ~ -0.9% perf but with tail-token instability, INT8 ~ -1.3%, AWQ ~ -2.1%

zara: the L40S FP8 runs exhibit low-probability token flips after ~4k tokens; not catastrophic but visible in beam traces. logs attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/rwdbakeoff/abcd1234

maya: when you say "token flips" — do you mean repeated attention weights collapse or sudden logit spikes?

zara: sudden logit spikes on very rare tokens, often at sentence boundaries. trace shows attention norms suddenly drop ~0.7x, then logits get noisy. H100 FP8 doesn't show this.

kevin: could be a kernel alpha scaling mismatch — L40S FP8 kernels we shipped last week had a slightly different activation scaling heuristic. infra-bot: kernel-rollout v2.14 applied to l40s-pool at 1990010600.

samir: any perf counters or profiler snapshots?

zara: yes — profiler snapshot attached. snippet: 
```
[profiler] device=l40s, step=4123, attn_norm_mean=0.021 -> 0.015, kv_cache_hits=0.99, avg_logit_norm=4.2 -> 6.1 (spike)
```

maya: this smells like mixed-precision accumulation mismatch when using continuous batching + KV cache warmup. did you enable accumulation->fp32 checkpointing?

zara: we used runtime default (accum fp16 paths). enabling fp32 accumulation reduces noise but increases latency by ~6ms/token on L40S.

kevin: for rollout plan: 1) add a kernel flag to force fp32 accumulation on L40S for sequences > 4096; 2) add a canary that runs longseq prompts each deploy; 3) add a quality regression alert on token-branch divergence > 0.5%

canary-bot: canary test failed on l40s-canary-03 — token-branch divergence 0.72% vs baseline at 1990011200. See dashboard: https://console.redwood/ci/canaries/1990011200

samir: good catch. zara, can you open a minimal PR with kernel-flag and a small unit test that reproduces the spike? put the benchmark artifact link and the profiler json in the PR.

zara: will do. also prototyped a mitigation: clip attention logits by running a per-head scaling squeeze after softmax prep: 
```
for head in heads:
  qk = q @ k.T / sqrt(dk)
  scale = clamp(var(qk), 0.8, 1.2)
  qk *= (1.0/scale)
```
this reduced spikes in local runs but needs perf review.

maya: add that as opt-in runtime config behind --fp8-stability-mode so we can A/B.

kevin: once PR is up, patch release to canary pool and run overnight sweeps. if stable, roll to dedicated; if not, route L40S -> H100 for long-seq workloads by policy.

zara: noted. PR target: changelist/rlw-quant-fix. artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/rlw/1990011223. i'll tag you all in PR. thanks :thumbsup: 

samir: one more ask — add a small eval set that checks commonsense continuity at 6k tokens. we should catch these deltas earlier.

zara: added to tests/longseq_continuity.yaml in the PR.

kevin: great thread. summary action items: zara PR + kernel flag, maya config toggle, canary sweep, add longseq continuity eval. i'll create the rollout ticket. :eyes:
